arbitrary_nonforced_prime_injection.statement: for every odd prime q other than 3 and 5, and every m>=1, (A,B,C)=(q^m,3,4) is a full Q_q-local four-square endpoint
checks: A^2+B^2=q^(2m)+9 is a Q_q square because its unit residue is 9
A^2+C^2=q^(2m)+16 is a Q_q square because its unit residue is 16
A^2+B^2+C^2=q^(2m)+25 is a Q_q square because its unit residue is 25
arbitrary_nonforced_prime_injection.consequence: arbitrarily large odd primes can enter an edge with either valuation parity without a local obstruction from the four-square equations

exact_boundary.reason_squareclass_not_closed: forced-prime parity is free and arbitrary nonforced odd primes can enter edge squareclasses locally; no theorem bounds global odd-prime support or valuation parity
